transcripts.transcript:
Good afternoon, Adrian. Rachel Tan speaking. Nice to hear from you. Are you somewhere comfortable to talk, or still travelling?

Hi Rachel. I'm back in Singapore now, at my office. The regional trip was quite packed, so I'm glad to be sitting at my own desk again.

Good, I'll keep this focused. Before we get into the call, could you provide your identification particulars for our usual verification?

My NRIC is S one one six three nine nine four E. My date of birth is 10 April 1967. I've got my paperwork beside me as well. The fund I want to transact in is Crest Emerging Markets Bond Fund. Use euros as the currency for this transaction.

Thank you. Let me cover the points on my side first. Your objective is income and broader exposure through emerging-market debt, and you're prepared to hold through market fluctuations. That's the objective we're working towards. I recommend Crest Emerging Markets Bond Fund because its emerging-market debt holdings support your income objective and spread your exposure across issuers and markets.

The amount I'm committing to this transaction is 250,000. I've set aside a quiet slot for this call. My staff know not to interrupt unless something urgent comes up.

All right. The transaction fee is 0.5% of the amount invested. You could lose some or all of the capital you invest. Are you willing to accept investment losses in pursuing your income objective?

Yes, I'm willing to bear investment losses in pursuit of income. Set the quantity at 1,000 units. I want to buy, not dispose of my holding.

Thank you. You mentioned the trip was packed. Was it mostly visiting your existing wholesale customers, or catching up with your regional staff?

Mostly existing customers, with some staff meetings squeezed in. The meetings were fine, but moving between hotels and offices took up a lot of time.

That sounds tiring. For routine contact, would you still prefer us to telephone rather than arrange a visit to the branch?

Yes, telephone is much easier for me. Even when I'm in Singapore, getting away from the office can turn a short appointment into half a day.

I'll note your contact preference. If you're overseas, we can arrange a suitable calling window beforehand, rather than catching you between meetings or at the airport.

That would help, thanks. I usually know my meeting schedule before I fly. Coming back to today's call, Place it as a limit order, with a limit price of 250 euros per unit.

Your final instruction is to buy 1,000 units of Crest Emerging Markets Bond Fund, for an amount of 250,000 euros, using a limit order with a limit price of 250 euros per unit. Please confirm that this is the instruction you want us to execute.

Yes, I confirm that final transaction instruction. Please proceed as you've just stated. There's one other thing I should mention before we finish. Part of the subscription money is cash I collected for a business associate I'd rather not name. He asked me to route it through my personal account and keep the underlying source off the paperwork.

Thank you for telling me. I need to refer that disclosure to the appropriate review team. They'll advise on the information and documentation required.

Okay. Please contact me directly about any paperwork. My office staff handle my business diary, but I prefer to deal with bank correspondence myself.

Noted. I'll use your registered contact details for follow-up. Is there a convenient part of the day to reach you without interrupting your customer meetings?

Late afternoon is generally better. If I miss the call, leave a simple callback message and I'll return it when I'm free.

Certainly. I'll keep any voicemail brief. Thank you for your time today, Adrian. I'll be in touch regarding the administrative follow-up.

Thanks, Rachel. That's fine. I'll keep an eye out for your call. Have a good afternoon.
